'''Anatoly V. Zayats''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|MAE|FInstP|FRSC}} is a British [[Experimental physics|experimental physicist]] of [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] origin known for his work in [[nanophotonics]], [[plasmonics]], [[metamaterial]]s and applied [[nanotechnology]].<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref>  He is currently a Chair in Experimental Physics and the head of the Photonics & Nanotechnology Group<ref>{{cite web|title=Photonics & Nanotechnology Group|url=https://www.kcl.ac.uk/nms/depts/physics/research/PN/GroupMembers.aspx|website=King's College London|accessdate=19 December 2017}}</ref> at [[King's College London]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Department of Physics|url=https://www.kcl.ac.uk/nms/depts/physics/people/academicstaff/zayats.aspx|website=King's College London|accessdate=18 July 2017}}</ref> He is a co-director of the [[London Centre for Nanotechnology]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Directors |url=https://www.london-nano.com/our-people/directors |website=London Centre for Nanotechnology |accessdate=5 September 2018}}</ref> and the London Institute for Advanced Light Technologies<ref>{{cite web |title=Directors |url=http://london-light.org/people/|website=London Institute for Advanced Light Technologies |accessdate=22 September 2020}}</ref>

==Education==
Zayats was educated at the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]].{{cn|date=October 2026}}

== Career and research ==
Zayats's current research interests are in areas of [[nanophotonics]], [[plasmonics]] and [[metamaterials]], optical spin-orbit effects and topological photonics, [[nonlinear optics|nonlinear]] and ultrafast optics and [[spectroscopy]],  photo-active nanomaterials, [[scanning probe microscopy]] and optical properties of surfaces, thin films, semiconductors and low-dimensional structures.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anatoly Zayats |url=https://www.london-nano.com/our-people/our-people-bios/anatoly-zayats |website=London Centre for Nanotechnology |access-date=20 April 2023}}</ref>

Zayats may be most widely-known for his contributions to the development of nano-optics of surface plasmon polaritons, nonlinear plasmonics and nanophotonics, hyperbolic and epsilon-near-zero metamaterials and their applications in ultrasensitive bio- and chemical sensing and nonlinear optics, plasmonic hot-electrons for photochemical transformations as well photonic spin-orbit effects in nanophotonics for directional routing of guided modes, directional optical forces and discovery of photonic skyrmions.

Zayats currently leads the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] programme grant 'New perspectives in photocatalysis and near-surface chemistry: catalysis meets plasmonics'<ref>{{cite web |title=CPLAS – New perspectives in photocatalysis and near-surface chemistry |url=https://www.cplas.org/ |website=www.cplas.org |access-date=21 April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=New perspectives in photocatalysis and near-surface chemistry: catalysis meets plasmonics |url=https://gow.epsrc.ukri.org/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=EP/W017075/1 |website=EPSRC Grants on Web |access-date=20 April 2023}}</ref> (2022-2028) (CPLAS), investigating light-driven energy-conversion at the nanoscale for stimulating chemical transformations. This is a multidisciplinary collaborative project between [[King's College London]], [[Imperial College London]] and the UK Catalysis Hub. CPLAS is the third EPSRC programme grant that Zayats has led; Active Plasmonics<ref>{{cite web |title=Research Staff|url=https://www.activeplasmonics.org/research-staff.php|website=Active Plasmonics |accessdate=22 September 2020}}</ref> ran from 2009 to 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=Active Plasmonics |url=https://gow.epsrc.ukri.org/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=EP/H000917/2 |website=gow.epsrc.ukri.org |language=en}}</ref> and Reactive Plasmonics,<ref>{{cite web |title=Our People |url=https://reactiveplasmonics.org/people-2/ |website=Reactive Plasmonics}}</ref> from 2015 to 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Reactive Plasmonics |url=https://gow.epsrc.ukri.org/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=EP/M013812/1 |website=gow.epsrc.ukri.org |language=en}}</ref>

Zayats is the holder of the ERC Advanced Grants Integrated Plasmonic Metamaterials<ref>{{cite web|title=Frontiers in nanophotonics: integrated plasmonic metamaterials devices |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/321268 |website=European Research Council|accessdate=22 September 2020}}</ref> (2013-2018) and Integrating Complex Beams and Metasurfaces.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of Principal Investigators |url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc_2017_adg_results_pe.pdf |website=European Research Council|accessdate=22 September 2020}}</ref>(2018-2023).

In 2017, together with Stefan Maier (Imperial College London) and [[Franco Cacialli]] (UCL), he founded the London Institute for Advanced Light Technologies,<ref>{{cite web |title=London Light|url=http://london-light.org/|website=London Institute for Advanced Light Technologies |accessdate=22 September 2020}}</ref> a joint virtual research centre between [[King's College London]], [[Imperial College London]] and [[University College London]].

Zayats is a founding co-editor-in-chief of the [[SPIE]]-Chinese Laser Press journal Advanced Photonics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Advanced Photonics|url=https://www.spiedigitallibrary.org/journals/Advanced-Photonics|website=advanced-photonics |accessdate=22 September 2020}}</ref>

===Publications===
Zayats's research has been published in leading [[peer review]]ed [[scientific journal]]s.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref>
